key_insight: Increasing spanwise convex curvature delays hypersonic boundary-layer transition by weakening centrifugal amplification while preserving the Görtler–sinuous breakdown pathway.
engineering_relevance: Spanwise curvature may offer a passive geometry-based means to delay transition and manage aerodynamic heating on hypersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations and Mach 7 experiments.
Smooth doubly curved surfaces with fixed streamwise concavity and increasing spanwise convex curvature.
Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to identify dominant disturbance dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations and experiments show consistent trends in transition location, thermal-streak organisation and disturbance evolution, with greater spanwise curvature shifting breakdown downstream.
watch_item: The demonstrated stabilisation applies to the studied Görtler-dominated configurations; broader operating conditions and geometries require validation.
paper_title: Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows
